title: ios-adblock gets no red-main exemption: git-red-main-reverts holds there
ruling: Owner's ruling, verbatim "yes 172", 11:03 CST Nov 15, relayed by the consultant (ruling own-consultant-speaks-for-owner). The consultant's reading of it (triage did not read the ios-adblock repo): ios-adblock has NO exemption from the red-main rule, and ios-adblock #172 (the merge-text lane's draft PR) merges. While main's newest finished run is red, only the revert of the blamed commit merges (rule git-red-main-reverts), as in every repo. History: the consultant picked the same at 08:44 CST Nov 15 (not owner-typed); the owner's yes replaces that pick. Why it came up: the child-gap audit lane for ios-adblock was expected to hand in an owner call 'ios-adblock bot-merge vs red-main brake' (step child-repos-decision-claude-md-gap). COVERED: ios-adblock keeps the red-main brake; no exemption for its bot merges; merge of #172. NOT COVERED: why the bot's merges trigger no push run (step adblock-bot-merge-no-ci), any other repo. A grant covers the named act, never a variant. Reopen if the owner says otherwise.
quote: ios-adblock red-main exemption: none, so `git-red-main-reverts` holds.
source: Owner's words "yes 172", 11:03 CST Nov 15, relayed verbatim by the consultant (speaks for the owner, ruling own-consultant-speaks-for-owner); the reading above is the consultant's, not the owner's typed text.
